findings.title: UsernameForm calls a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` evaluates `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method introduced by this PR is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160) and neither `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` nor `AbstractFormAuthenticator` declares a no-arg variant. As written this does not compile. If the intent was the realm-level check, a parameterless helper has to be added; if the intent was the user-aware check, it must be called as `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, disabling conditional-UI passkeys on the anonymous login page
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It is used as the gate for `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in the error `challenge()` override (line 137). Before this change the fill was executed exactly in the opposite situation (`context.getUser() == null`), i.e. for the normal, not-yet-identified login. With the new gate, the first login page (user == null) no longer gets the WebAuthn challenge/RP-ID/conditional-UI attributes, so passkey conditional UI / autofill login is silently turned off for regular logins — the very feature this class implements. This also contradicts existing assertions in the test suite, e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey asserts `//form[@id='webauth']` is present on the initial login page. The condition for the re-authentication case should be added without dropping the `user == null` case (e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && (user == null || userHasPasskey(user))`).

findings.title: Overriding shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to always false removes the "user has no passkey" guard
findings.body: In `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` the branch guarded by `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` also performs the check `if (authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()) return null;`, i.e. it signals that the identified user owns no WebAuthn credential of the required type. By hard-coding `false` here, that guard is never reached for the conditional-UI authenticator, so during re-authentication (where the user is already known) the passkey UI/conditional-UI attributes are emitted even for users that have no passkey credential at all. Those users are offered a "sign in with passkey" option that can only fail. Consider still inspecting the identified user's credentials and skipping the passkey setup when none exist (note that `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()` also ignores a `null` return from `fillContextForm`).

findings.title: SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS and ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS can now disagree
findings.body: `shouldDisplayAuthenticators(context)` still returns `context.getUser() != null`, while the newly extracted `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` is overridden to `false` in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`. During re-authentication (user != null, conditional UI) the form therefore gets `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS=true` but never gets the `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` bean, a combination that was impossible before (both flags were derived from `user != null`). Templates that use `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` to render the authenticator selection list will have no bean to iterate over, which at best renders an empty selector and at worst raises a FreeMarker reference error. `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` should be overridden consistently in the conditional-UI authenticator.

findings.title: Test comment claims to cover "user without passkey" but the realm policy disables passkeys entirely
findings.body: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so no passkey UI is rendered for any user in that realm; the inline comment "Passkeys login should not be available on the page as this user does not have passkey" describes a different scenario than the one actually exercised. The interesting (and newly changed) case — re-authentication of a user who has no passkey credential in a realm where the passkeys policy is enabled — is not covered by any test, even though the new `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() == false` override in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator changes exactly that behaviour. Please fix the comment and add a test with the passkeys policy enabled and a user without a passkey credential.

findings.title: try/fail/catch(Exception) for absent element can mask unrelated WebDriver failures
findings.body: The blocks at lines 291-296 and 312-317 assert absence of the webauthn form by calling `driver.findElement(...)` inside a `try` and catching plain `Exception`. Any WebDriver exception (stale element, timeout, broken page, session error) is treated as "element absent", so the assertion can pass for the wrong reason; the `assertThat(element, nullValue())` line can also never succeed. The same files already use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))` (e.g. PasskeysUsernameFormTest:202); use that instead so only the expected exception is accepted.
